passage.title: Our Amazing Bodies
paragraphs: Our bodies are amazing. Every day they work hard to keep us healthy. But everyone gets sick sometimes. You can’t see germs with your bare eyes, but they make you sick. Some germs can live for two hours on your desk. So use tissues when you sneeze or cough! And wash your hands with soap.

passage.title: The Twilight Zone
paragraphs: There’s a lot of sunlight in the sunlit zone, the top layer of the ocean, but there isn’t much light in the twilight zone. Where the sunlit zone ends, at 200 meters (650 feet), the twilight zone begins. It goes down to about 1,000 meters (3,300 feet).

The twilight zone is cold and dark. But that doesn’t keep animals from living here. Most fish in this zone are small, but some of the biggest ocean animals also live here. Many of the fish in the twilight zone can make their own light. This helps them see, and it helps them catch and eat fish. It also makes the fish look strange. They can look very different from fish in the sunlit zone.

And now scientists think that the number of fish and other ocean animals that live here is much greater than they thought long ago. Up to ten times greater! This is good news because it means there is more ocean life in the twilight zone than we thought. The bad news is that fishing companies are looking for ways to fish in the twilight zone. Someday fishing companies may kill so many fish that not enough fish are left to reproduce. We must study and protect the ocean life in the twilight zone.

parts.name: Speaking with Dad
parts.sub: Dad asks, you answer out loud. 1 point each.
parts.imageAlt: Covered wagons pulled by teams of horses and mules, with riders beside them, crossing a grassy hillside long ago.
parts.caption: Look at the picture while Dad asks you.

prompts.q: How did children use to go to school?
What is faster than a horse?
prompts.a: A car is faster than a horse.

prompts.q: Compare travel long ago and today.
prompts.a: Long ago people used horses and wagons. Today they use cars instead.

prompts.q: What is the fastest way to travel today?
prompts.a: An airplane is the fastest way to travel today.

prompts.q: Now let’s talk about you and your ideas about traveling. Tell me a place that you would like to travel to.
prompts.a: I would like to travel to Hawaii. / I would like to travel to London.

prompts.q: Tell me how you have to travel there.
prompts.a: You have to take an airplane. / You have to take a train.

prompts.q: Tell me what you should take with you on your trip.
prompts.a: I should take an umbrella with me. / I should take a swimsuit and sunglasses with me.

prompts.q: Is there a person in your family who would like to go with you?
prompts.a: My mother is the person who would like to go with me.

prompts.q: What is one thing you would like to eat on vacation?
prompts.a: I’d like to eat ice cream.

prompts.q: What happens the longer you stay on vacation?
prompts.a: The longer I stay away from home on vacation, the more my family will miss me.
